reports.bigPicture:
Twenty-five years today.

I was three. No memory of towers or flight numbers, just one scene: my parents pulling me out of school early, no explanation given.

So I won't pretend to remember something I don't. But I've done the math on it since, and the math is what got me. Almost 3,000 people went to work on a Tuesday that looked exactly like every other Tuesday. Kissed their kid goodbye, or didn't even get the chance to. Assumed, the way you have to assume to function, that the ordinary version of the day was the one they'd get.

I've got a toddler now, and that's the part that sticks with me on this day.

I don't remember 9/11. But I do remember what it cost people, and I remember to take a moment for the ones who ran toward it that day instead of away.
reports.macroGrind:
We are in a very interesting part of the market (it’s always interesting that’s why we do this). With our new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, he has been very adamant that he will give no guidance and that he will listen to the markets. With the caveat that he is very serious about inflation. "We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do.”

Which is guidance…

But let’s move past that point real quick.

Essentially Warsh is telling the market that he is watching inflation, and he is telling the market that the forward progression of inflation will dictate rates.

NOW the market does not know how to model inflation.

Luckily everyone reading this right now is subscribed to Hedgeye. Our macro policy is Growth + Inflation = policy. AND we have the streets best inflation forecast…

That puts us at a special spot in this market. Others are reacting to something they don’t know what the direction is.

So, let’s get to the numbers.

Our nowcast, which comes out weekly AND projects out inflation a full month ahead of the print, has inflation for August as an acceleration. We actually have it at 3.5%. The market is at low 3.4% (meaning somewhere between 3.36% - 3.43%). Previous month inflation was 3.36%. So, both Hedgeye and the market have an acceleration, Hedgeye is seeing a larger acceleration than the street, but importantly an acceleration. THEN we have to look one month out to September, Hedgeye has another acceleration of ~10bps from the August number. The street: has inflation flat. THEN looking at the Q4/December inflation, Hedgeye has inflation essentially flat from there (sticky high). The street: has no forecast.

Which means we have to remember, since the market does not have an accurate nowcast they are reacting to whatever just happens. They are blind. We at Hedgeye have a sneak peek at what they are going to see. Which is: accelerating and sticky high inflation for the rest of the year.

Now, we use that to front run fed policy. Which is pretty simple, a higher probability of rate hikes into the end of the year.

You don’t have to listen to me on that, listen to the market. The 2yr yield (the fed front runner) has been making cycle highs and higher highs within a bullish trend and trade. One of the most bullish signals you can have in macro (bullish from a yield perspective).

We have to remember though that the market isn’t really looking much further than past this next inflation print and the Fed meeting next week. That is where you at Hedgeye can front run the market.

But what is important is to listen to the market while it continues to price in more rate hikes due to their perception of higher inflation. What has worked very well from a performance standpoint: Commodities (Oil and Agg), Energy stocks, Long rates (short bonds), select international exposures.

What has worked very poorly: Russell, Growth, Momentum, Industrials, Retail, China Technology, Bonds, Utilities.

It is no coincidence that this is what our positioning is. We have been getting longer of inflation, select intl. exposures (like Colombia COLO). While getting shorter of momentum, growth, Bonds, and Utes.

Always remember, this is a pendulum that swings. The market loves to price in more rate hikes than what will actually happen and then swing back to the other side and price in more rate cuts than will actually happen. Why is it a pendulum? Because the market doesn’t actually have a model, it is going off of what happened last and projecting out that as the future.

When this pendulum swings in the other direction we will tell you, the market signals will change, and we will change alongside it. But for now, long inflation is where the alpha is and what we are currently riding.

We will follow the process. Going into today’s inflation print, Crude Oil and Rates were at the top ends of their ranges. Meaning we already got paid shorting bonds and XLU going into today already. We sold some at the top end of the range and Keith currently has these positions at his min. Now we are in wait and watch mode to see what yields signal on the leaked “news” of inflation.

, Hedgeye CEO and Risk-Manager-In-Chief Keith McCullough broke down the rising probability of back-to-back Monthly #Quad2s (inflation and growth both accelerating) as Hedgeye's Inflation Nowcast ticked higher for both September and October.

									Buying Physical Gold & Silver: Who We Trust 



Precious metals aren’t a side story anymore. They’re one of the biggest macro stories in global markets. 



Gold and silver have experienced extraordinary moves over the past year as investors have grappled with persistent inflation risk, gargantuan government debt loads, currency volatility and growing questions about the long-term purchasing power of fiat money. 



But the move hasn’t been straight up. Nor should investors expect it to be. That’s precisely why process matters more than prediction. 



At Hedgeye, we don’t believe in blindly buying an asset because there’s a compelling long-term story behind it. Price, timing and risk management still matter.
